question: Why does the selected faction package fail the provisional winning-path entropy floor: excessive Adoption scoring, support lanes hidden by the classifier, deterministic policy preference, or a genuine lack of viable winning identities?
requiredDiagnostics: winner share by classified path and supported player count
Core Action selections by winning path
mean Capability, Customers, Facilities, Trust, and Mandate by winning path
faction, persona, backend, and World Ending composition by winning path
all enforced balance checks and integrity signals

interpretationRules.scoring: A rule probe is eligible only if one Mandate source is disproportionately concentrated in the dominant winning path and the current value can plausibly explain the observed advantage.
interpretationRules.classifier: If support lanes contribute materially to winners but are hidden by exclusive path labels, fix the diagnostic rather than the physical game.
interpretationRules.policy: If the concentration is isolated to one persona or backend, diagnose policy and counterplay before changing rules.
interpretationRules.global: No global economy, Customer, Capability, Trust, AGI, Grid-Ready, Research, or Realignment change may be selected directly from this diagnostic.
interpretationRules.promotion: Any physical candidate requires a later one-lever preregistration on fresh common seeds, a tracked receipt, synchronized surfaces, explicit user approval, and physical testing.
